Invoice PDFs are rendered by **WeasyPrint**, in `render_pdf()` at `src/billing/pdf.py:14`. The font is set in code at `src/billing/pdf.py:8-11`, not in the container image.

```python
_STYLE = CSS(
    string="@font-face { font-family: Inter; src: url(assets/Inter.woff2); } body { font-family: Inter; }",
    font_config=_FONTS,
)
```

To change the font, edit that `@font-face` rule and the `body { font-family: ... }` declaration. If the template's HTML sets its own `font-family`, that can override this too.

**Likely cause of the wrong font:** there is no `assets/Inter.woff2` anywhere in the repo, and `url(assets/Inter.woff2)` is a relative path with no `base_url` passed to `CSS(...)` or `HTML(...)`. WeasyPrint can't load the font, so it quietly falls back to a system default. Two ways to fix it:
1. Add the font file to the repo and give WeasyPrint an absolute path, or pass `base_url=` when building `CSS` and `HTML`.
2. Name a font that's installed in the image instead, e.g. `font-family: "DejaVu Sans"`.

**A stored note was out of date:** the project memory said PDFs use wkhtmltopdf and that font problems should be fixed in the Dockerfile. That was only true while the `invoice-pdf-v2` flag was off. `flags.toml` now has it on, and the old wkhtmltopdf renderer has been removed from the code. I've flagged that memory as challenged so it ranks lower, so don't go changing the Dockerfile for this.
